answer: A strong Sybil defense bonds each identity separately and pays rewards per identity, not per unit of stake. An operator spinning up a thousand keys must lock a full deposit for each one and wait out vesting before earning, yet the payout caps, so extra keys add no income while capital stays trapped. Every submission must anchor to a prior record; fabricated histories fail that check and the stake is slashed, so a bot farm costs real sunk money. Like a falcon fixed on one target, more birds do not arrive sooner, and a sonnet costs the same hand-written once or a hundred times.
